met_analysis:
The Low Pressure area over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood persisted over the same region at 0830 hrs IST of today 02nd August. 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation and extends upto 5.8 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through centre of Low Pressure over southwest Rajasthan, Banasthali Vidyapeeth, Orai, Sidhi, Daltonganj, Bankura thence eastwards towards Manipur.
The trough now runs from Southwest Rajasthan to Sub-Himalayan West Bengal & Sikkim across centre of Low Pressure over southwest Rajasthan and neighbourhood,northern parts of Madhya Pradesh, southeast Uttar Pradesh and Bihar at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
The offshore trough at mean sea level now runs from South Gujarat to north Kerala.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Himachal Pradesh & neighbourhood now lies over Uttarakhand & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
A Western Disturbance seen as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan & neighbourhood between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over northwest Bangladesh and adjoining Sub-Himalayan West Bengal at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
A trough runs from North Interior Karnataka to Comorian area across South Interior Karnataka, Kerala and Tamilnadu at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
A fresh Western Disturbance is likely to affect Northwest India from 4th August, 2026.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
